---
title: "The 3-Tier Resolver Guide"
subtitle: "Models evaluate physics. Solvers find limits. Optimizers search for trade-offs."
---

```{python}
#| echo: false
#| output: false
import mlsysim
import mlsysim.solvers
_n_solvers = sum(1 for n in mlsysim.solvers.__all__ if not n.startswith("Base") and n != "ForwardModel")
```

MLSys·im provides **`{python} f"{_n_solvers}"` concrete resolvers** covering the [22 Systems Walls](architecture.qmd) across six core domains (**Node**, **Data**, **Algorithm**, **Fleet**, **Ops**, and **Analysis**) plus chapter-specific resolvers across **Volumes I–IV** (including **Agentic AI** and **Physical AI / Robotics**). See the [Textbook & Chapter Map](curriculum-map.qmd) for how each resolver aligns with textbook chapters and study sheets.

To make engineering decisions systematic, the tools are organized into a **3-Tier Architecture**:

```{mermaid}
%%{init: {'theme': 'neutral'}}%%
flowchart LR
    A["<b>1. Analytical Models</b><br/><i>Y = f(X)</i><br/><span style='font-size:0.8em;color:#666;'>Evaluate consequences</span>"]
    B["<b>2. Analysis Solvers</b><br/><i>X = f⁻¹(Y)</i><br/><span style='font-size:0.8em;color:#666;'>Find exact limits</span>"]
    C["<b>3. Optimizers (DSE)</b><br/><i>max f(X)</i><br/><span style='font-size:0.8em;color:#666;'>Search design space</span>"]

    A --> B
    A --> C

    style A fill:#e0f2fe,stroke:#0284c7,stroke-width:2px
    style B fill:#fef08a,stroke:#d97706
    style C fill:#dcfce3,stroke:#10b981
```

1. **Analytical Models (`*Model`)**: The Physics Engine. Given a configuration, evaluate the consequences ($Y = f(X)$).
2. **Analysis Solvers (`*Solver`)**: The Math Engine. Given a target, algebraically solve for the required input ($X = f^{-1}(Y)$).
3. **Optimizers (`*Optimizer`)**: The Engineering Engine. Search a design space to maximize or minimize an objective ($\max f(X)$).

::: {.callout-tip}
## Quick Start
Use `Engine.solve()` for generic single-device Roofline analysis. Use a specialized solver when the question requires its accounting, such as KV-aware decode in `ServingModel`. See [Choosing a Python API](choosing-an-api.qmd) for executable examples and the scope of scenarios.
:::

---

## 1. Analytical Models (The Physics Engine)

These models answer the question *"What happens if I run this exact setup?"*

### Domain 1: Node (Single-Accelerator Resources)
| Model | Key Inputs | Key Outputs | Best For |
|:------|:-----------|:------------|:---------|
| [**`SingleNodeModel`**](api/solvers.SingleNodeModel.qmd) | model, hardware, batch_size | latency, throughput, bottleneck | "Is my model memory-bound?" |
| [**`TrainingMemoryModel`**](api/solvers.TrainingMemoryModel.qmd) | model, hardware, batch_size, seq_len | weights, gradients, optimizer, activations | "Why does training need so much more memory?" |
| [**`EfficiencyModel`**](api/solvers.EfficiencyModel.qmd) | model, hardware, workload_type | mfu, achievable FLOP/s | "What MFU will my workload achieve?" |
| [**`ServingModel`**](api/solvers.ServingModel.qmd) | model, hardware, seq_len | TTFT, ITL, KV-cache footprint, decode stall proxy | "Can I serve this LLM on this GPU?" |
| [**`ServingCapacityModel`**](api/solvers.ServingCapacityModel.qmd) | model, hardware, QPS, target P99 | replicas, capacity, queue wait | "How many replicas do I need for this SLA?" |
| [**`ContinuousBatchingModel`**](api/solvers.ContinuousBatchingModel.qmd) | model, hardware, max_seq_len, mean_request_tokens, page_size | static vs paged capacity, internal fragmentation, speedup vs static | "How much concurrency does paging buy over static KV reservation?" |
| [**`WeightStreamingModel`**](api/solvers.WeightStreamingModel.qmd) | model, hardware, seq_len, batch_size | throughput_tokens_per_sec, optimal_batch_size | "Cerebras wafer-scale inference?" |
| [**`TailLatencyModel`**](api/solvers.TailLatencyModel.qmd) | arrival_rate_qps, service_latency_ms, num_replicas | p50_latency, p99_latency, queue_utilization | "Will I meet P99 total latency SLAs?" |

### Domain 6: Agentic & Cyber-Physical Systems
Beyond single-node and datacenter fleet models, `mlsysim.solvers` exports specialized first-principles resolvers for multi-turn agent harnesses and closed-loop embodied machines (documented in full in the [API Reference](api/index.qmd) and [Scenarios by Domain](api/scenario-domains.qmd)):

| Representative Model | Key Inputs | Key Outputs | Best For |
|:---------------------|:-----------|:------------|:---------|
| [**`HorizonCompoundingModel`**](api/engine.solvers.agents.qmd) | step_success, horizons, target_success, target_horizon | step_error, success, required_step_error, first_horizon_below_target | "How fast does per-step error compound across an agent horizon?" |
| [**`AcceptedTaskCostModel`**](api/engine.solvers.agents.qmd) | model_cost, other_cost, acceptance | attempt_cost, attempts_per_acceptance, cost_per_accepted | "What is the dollar cost per verified solved task?" |
| [**`AppendOnlyContextModel`**](api/engine.solvers.agents.qmd) | initial_tokens, tokens_per_turn, turns, context_window | last_call_tokens, cumulative_input_tokens, reread_ratio | "How quadratically does append-only agent history bill tokens?" |
| [**`StoppingBudgetModel`**](api/engine.solvers.embodied.qmd) | speed, delay, deceleration, clear_distance | delay_travel, braking_travel, stop_distance, spare, fits | "Can a robot or vehicle stop inside its perception horizon?" |
| [**`PhaseLagBudgetModel`**](api/engine.solvers.realtime.qmd) | crossover, sample_period, compute_delay, transport_delay, phase_allowance | total_delay, phase_total, delay_margin, fits | "Does inference latency destabilize a closed-loop controller?" |
| [**`EtherCatCycleModel`**](api/engine.solvers.realtime.qmd) | num_axes, bytes_per_axis, baud_rate, header_bytes, hop_delay, cycle | frame_time, occupancy, utilization, fits | "Will my fieldbus meet a 1 kHz deterministic control deadline?" |

## 2. Analysis Solvers (The Math Engine)

These solvers answer the question *"What exact number do I need to hit my target?"*

| Solver | Key Inputs | Key Outputs | Best For |
|:-------|:-----------|:------------|:---------|
| [**`SensitivitySolver`**](api/solvers.SensitivitySolver.qmd) | model, hardware, perturbation_pct | sensitivities, binding_constraint | "Which parameter should I invest in?" |
| [**`SynthesisSolver`**](api/solvers.SynthesisSolver.qmd) | model, target_latency | required_bw, required_flops | "What hardware do I need for this SLA?" |

---

## 3. Optimizers & Design Space Exploration (DSE)

Domain optimizers (`ParallelismOptimizer`, `BatchingOptimizer`, `PlacementOptimizer`) search standard configurations directly, while the general-purpose `DSE` engine sweeps arbitrary multi-dimensional parameter grids under explicit user constraints.

| Engine | Key Inputs | Objective | Best For |
|:----------|:-----------|:----------|:---------|
| [**`DSE Engine`**](api/engine.dse.DSE.qmd) | search space, objective, constraints | minimize/maximize | "What max batch size is safe for my SLA?" or "Where should I build my datacenter?" |

---

## Composing Resolvers

Real-world questions require **chaining** multiple tiers. Here are three common patterns:

### Sizing and costing an H100 serving fleet for Llama-3 8B

```{python}
from mlsysim import Hardware, Models, Q_
from mlsysim.solvers import ServingCapacityModel, EconomicsModel
from mlsysim.systems.types import Fleet, Node, NetworkFabric

capacity = ServingCapacityModel().solve(
    model=Models.Language.Llama3_8B,
    hardware=Hardware.Cloud.H100,
    qps=40.0,
    target_p99_latency_ms=1500.0,
    max_seq_len=4096,
    mean_request_tokens=1024,
    output_tokens=128,
)
nodes_needed = (capacity.required_replicas + 7) // 8
fleet = Fleet(
    name="Serving-H100",
    node=Node(
        name="8xH100",
        accelerator=Hardware.Cloud.H100,
        accelerators_per_node=8,
        intra_node_bw=Q_("450 GB/s"),
    ),
    count=nodes_needed,
    fabric=NetworkFabric(name="IB-NDR", bandwidth=Q_("50 GB/s")),
)
cost = EconomicsModel().solve(fleet=fleet, duration_days=365, kwh_price=0.08)
print(f"Replicas needed: {capacity.required_replicas} GPUs ({nodes_needed} node(s)), P99: {capacity.estimated_p99_latency:~.0f}")
print(f"Annual TCO:      ${cost.tco_usd:,.0f} (CapEx ${cost.capex_usd:,.0f} + OpEx ${cost.total_opex_usd:,.0f})")
```

### The parameter that matters most for Llama-8B latency

```{python}
from mlsysim import Hardware, Models
from mlsysim.solvers import SensitivitySolver

sensitivity = SensitivitySolver().solve(
    model=Models.Language.Llama3_8B,
    hardware=Hardware.Cloud.H100,
    precision="fp16",
    perturbation_pct=10.0
)
print(f"Binding constraint: {sensitivity.binding_constraint}")
print(f"BW sensitivity:     {sensitivity.sensitivities['memory_bandwidth']:+.3f}")
print(f"FLOPS sensitivity:  {sensitivity.sensitivities['peak_flops']:+.3f}")
```

### The hardware a 50ms SLA requires

```{python}
from mlsysim import Models
from mlsysim.solvers import SynthesisSolver
from mlsysim.core.units import Q_

synthesis = SynthesisSolver().solve(
    model=Models.Language.Llama3_8B,
    target_latency=Q_("50 ms"),
    precision="fp16"
)
print(f"Required bandwidth: {synthesis.required_bw.to('TB/s'):~.2f}")
print(f"Required FLOPS:     {synthesis.required_flops.to('TFLOPs/s'):~.1f}")
```
